brique._comment: Engine-native Matter family capacity. kind/wrapper/rel_ctx/lang do not apply here.

objective.name: matter.write
objective.description: Patch one existing matter, apply terminal semantic value add/remove operations, and optionally update its brique-managed substance.

#root.role: Merge metadata patches, optionally write inline or leased substance data, and commit the updated matter revision.

matter_id._comment: Required. Name of the matter to write within the addressed context.

expected_revision._comment: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard. When supplied, it must be a positive integer (or its base-10 string representation) equal to the matter's current revision. JSON integer tokens are decoded without float64 precision loss. The comparison is performed while holding the per-matter lock; a mismatch refuses the write before any metadata or substance mutation. Omit this parameter to retain unconditional last-write-wins behavior. Legacy aliases exp_rev and expected_rev remain accepted.

meaning._comment: Optional. Replacement for the meaning descriptor section.

functional._comment: Optional. Replacement for the functional descriptor section.

brique._comment: Optional. Replacement for the brique descriptor section.

semantic_patch._comment: Optional atomic semantic patch. Canonical form: { operations: [{ op: 'set'|'add'|'remove'|'delete'|'insert'|'test', path: (string|non-negative integer)[], value?: any }] }. Numeric segments address arrays; string segments address object keys. delete omits value; all other ops require it. Legacy {add:[...], remove:[...]} remains accepted but cannot be mixed with operations. path[0] must be objective, subjective, functional, or brique; those root sections cannot be deleted or replaced by non-objects. semantic_patch never reaches matter substance/data; use params.data or an HTTP upload lease for business content.

data._comment: Optional small inline substance payload. Strings become raw bytes; other values are JSON-marshaled. Do not carry binary or voluminous content here, including as base64: request an HTTP upload lease with http_data=true instead. How matter.read later serializes small inline content (plain string vs base64) is controlled separately by brique.substance_type ('text', the default, or 'binary').

http_data._comment: Optional. Set to true for binary or voluminous substance data. The engine returns a one-shot HTTP PUT handle; the caller must begin the PUT before expires_at. The upload uses lease-unique temporary files, does not hold the matter lock while streaming, and acquires that lock only to verify the bound revision and finalize the commit. Accepted values: true (bool), 'true' or '1' (string), non-zero number.

revision._comment: New revision number after the write. Present on inline write path.

http_data._comment: Present only when params.http_data was true. HTTP write lease handle: { kind: 'http', base_url: string, path: string (e.g. '/substance/<rid>'), rid: string, tok: string, expires_at: integer (unix nanoseconds), revision: integer, method: 'PUT' }. The caller must begin the one-shot PUT to <base_url><path>?tok=<tok> before expires_at; an active upload may finish afterward. When present, revision is not included in the intention response because it is committed by the PUT response after upload finalization.

effects.matter_substance: data.bin may be replaced inline or via an HTTP lease when the matter stays in brique mode.
effects.subscriptions: Local brique subscribers may be notified after a successful commit.

transformation_contract.morphing: A matter identifier plus metadata or substance patches becomes a new committed matter revision, or an upload lease when the write is deferred through HTTP.
invariants: matter.write targets exactly one existing cataloged matter designated by matter_id.
Every committed revision is strictly greater than the matter's preceding revision, including when the wall clock does not advance or moves backwards.
When expected_revision is supplied, the current revision must match it under the per-matter lock before any mutation is staged.
semantic_patch operations execute in declared order on a clone; any failure rejects the complete patch without mutation. Numeric path segments traverse arrays.
Payload bytes are writable only when the addressed matter remains in brique substance mode.
Each HTTP upload lease owns unique temporary payload and descriptor files; the per-matter lock is acquired only at finalization.
success: A successful direct write returns ok=true, matter_id, and the committed revision.
A successful deferred write returns ok=true, matter_id, and an HTTP upload lease handle in http_data.
failure: The capacity fails when matter_id is missing, no patch intent is provided, or a patch payload has the wrong shape.
The capacity refuses the entire write with a revision-mismatch error when expected_revision differs from the current revision; no requested mutation is applied.
The capacity fails when payload writing is requested outside brique mode or when the commit boundary cannot be completed.
A deferred upload fails with a revision conflict when another write commits after the lease was opened and before it is finalized.
A descriptor-commit failure after payload replacement is reported explicitly as partial_commit.
The capacity fails with reason=invalid_patch, and applies none of the requested operations, when any semantic_patch op's path[0] is not one of objective, subjective, functional, brique.
notes: metadata patches are merged minimally into matter.json; semantic_patch.operations is the canonical precise mutation form and legacy add/remove remains accepted.

expected_revision is optional for direct writes: omitting it preserves unconditional serialized commits in lock-acquisition order. Deferred HTTP leases always bind finalization to the revision observed when the lease opens, so only a lease whose base revision is still current can commit.
Intentions are control-plane messages. Use inline data only for small content; all binary or voluminous content must use http_data and then be referenced as a matter.
Subscription notifications happen only after a successful committed write in brique mode.
